Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the agenda
during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments are limited to 3 minutes or less and
should be directed to City Council as a whole. Individuals are not permitted to extend, transfer, speak on behalf of others, or yield
their time to other speakers..

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Mayor Perez commented on the Mayor’s Clergy Meeting, reported on her attendance at
the Athens Services Irwindale Materials Recovery Facility Grand Opening and ribbon
cutting, ABC Adult School Outstanding Student Awards Ceremony, and the Egg-
Stravagant Egg Hunt; highlighted that Angela Tasker and Lidia Sanchez were recognized
by Assemblymember Blanca Pacheco for the 2026 Women of the Year; and encouraged
all to follow current events on the City’s Social Media. Vice Mayor Rios thanked staff for

dresses; and requested the meeting be adjourned in memory of Jose Ruben Barrios.

Fe Springs Award Luncheon April 19 at the Santa Fe Springs Town Center.

Competition Win. Videos were shared highlighting Opening Day 2026, Artastic 2026 and

Background:

The City’s fleet is a vital component in delivering essential services to the community and must
be maintained in a safe, reliable and cost-effective condition. The Vehicle Maintenance Division
establishes a Vehicle Useful Life Benchmark for each fleet unit, which defines its expected
service life and guides replacement decisions. This benchmark is based on factors such as age,
mileage, and maintenance costs.

To ensure the timely disposal of vehicles that no longer meet operational standards, the Finance
Department oversees the surplus process. Vehicles are sold at auction through the City’s
partner, JJ Kane, with the City typically receiving 80% to 90% of the final sale price after
commissions and fees. Prior to auction, the Vehicle Maintenance Division prepares each vehicle
by removing City decals, lights, and other installed equipment.

During fiscal year 2025/26, the City has surplused 10 vehicles, generating total proceeds of
$72,150. The cumulative value of vehicles surplused to date exceeds the current Purchasing
Authority Authorization Limit of $40,600 and therefore requires ratification by the City Council. In
accordance with Norwalk Municipal Code section 3.20.020 and related purchasing provisions,
any transaction exceeding the Purchasing Authority Authorization Limit requires City Council
approval. Attachment A includes all vehicles sold to date and their respective sale prices for
ratification.

In addition, 16 vehicles remain pending surplus, many of which are expected to be processed
before the end of the fiscal year. These vehicles also require City Council approval prior to

On July 15, 2025, City Council approved an agreement with Civiltec Engineering Inc. (“Civiltec”)
in the amount of $64,084 to provide professional construction support services for the Sewage
Lift Station Rehabilitation, City Project No. 7527 (“Project”) at Harvard Drive and Gridley Road.
These services include construction management, engineering support, and construction
inspection. The Project consists of rehabilitating an existing sewer lift station, including
installation of a temporary sewer bypass, removal and replacement of plug valves, swing check
valves, submersible pumps, slide rail assemblies, ductile iron piping, construction of a new meter
vault, and installation of a magnetic flow meter. Construction is anticipated to be completed by
Summer 2026.

During initial construction activities, staff identified that the existing alarm system at the lift station
is outdated and limited in functionality. To replace and upgrade the system, and to ensure
compatibility with a future Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, additional
design services are required.

provide professional engineering design services for the preparation of electrical plans and
specifications. These improvements will enhance alarm and notification capabilities, increase
the number of monitored alarm points, upgrade electrical components, and ensure compatibility
with the City’s future SCADA system. This work is in addition to the consultant’s existing
construction support services for the project. If approved, the design will be completed and
implemented by Summer 2026.
